leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open and the recommended action does not open one. The balance is comfortably positive and both parts of the move — setting the lineup and selling a player — only add to it. Every purchase considered this run was rejected in part because it would have required going temporarily negative and unwinding before the lock, and in the one case where the arithmetic worked the winning bid could not have been unwound at all. There is nothing outstanding that needs to be closed out before the deadline.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is the lineup, not the roster. The squad can already fill its best legal shape; it simply is not set to it. Nothing needs to be bought to close this gap and nothing needs to be sold first — the fix is free and available right now, and every hour it goes unapplied is an hour of avoidable risk that the lock arrives with the wrong eleven on the field. The secondary constraint is the number of legal sales rather than money: the spending-power figure is real for the floor rule but is not purchasing capacity, because cash is what actually has to cover a purchase and a negative balance at the lock scores nothing for the entire matchday.

verdict.detail: The top move has not changed and has still not been executed: set the lineup to 5-3-2 first, which brings Bernardo in and drops Amoako, and only then sell Amoako. That order matters — selling first would leave the squad at eleven with only ten placed and trigger the deletion penalty. The move costs nothing, needs no purchase, and is the whole of this cycle's action. This run's new work was to re-examine the board with a corrected spending ceiling, and the conclusion is that no purchase is worth making before the lock, though for a better-argued reason than last time.

sell.reason: Amoako remains the only points-free sale on the books and the case is unchanged and re-confirmed. Ligainsider's HSV page, still carrying its 01.09 timestamp, has him in the squad roster only — not in the projected eleven and not on the bench — and he is absent from the league-wide injury and suspension table, so this is a selection verdict rather than a fitness one. He has no points and no minutes on the board. Because the optimal shape already drops him, selling him leaves the fielded eleven completely untouched while banking his value, and his market value is decaying every couple of hours, so waiting has a small but real cost. Selling Widmer or Bernardo instead would both cost fielded points and neither is recommended.

Over the 45,6h to the lock that is roughly another 1,7M of decay on a 1,7M asset - selling now captures nearly all of what is left. Georg bought him at +79,18% over mv, the third-highest premium in the measured log, and is -1.790.553 on him; that loss is SUNK and is not a reason to hold a player who produces nothing. The other thing a 12th body buys is the option to bench Bernardo via 4-4-2 - but that option is worth ZERO points, because 4-4-2 without Bernardo is 1333 and 5-3-2 with a non-playing Bernardo is also 1333. The option only pays if there is someone GOOD to field instead, and there is not. SEQUENCING: set the lineup to 5-3-2 BEFORE selling, or the post-sale squad of 11 has only 10 placed. Not urgent against a deadline - it has until the 2026-09-04T18:30Z lock - but every two hours costs ~117k.

buy.reason: No purchase on this board improves the eleven before the lock, but one previous conclusion was wrong and is corrected here. Castello Jr. had been rejected by two earlier runs as simply unaffordable. He is not — the old ceiling wrongly treated Lokonga as unsellable because he is a quality hold, when in fact a purchase makes the squad thirteen and any two players may then be sold so long as the remaining eleven fills a legal shape. Re-priced properly by brute force over every listing, every legal unwind and all nine formations, he is affordable and is the only asset on the board that lifts the eleven at all. He is also genuinely good and genuinely available: fit per his profile retrieved today, named in Leipzig's projected eleven, a full ninety-seven minutes on matchday one, and the club has publicly backed away from selling him, so the exit risk is closed rather than open. He is still an avoid, for three reasons that are worth keeping. First, the apparent gain is an artefact of comparing one-match averages — re-priced at his multi-season mean the swap is a break-even, because his single big score is being measured against squad players whose numbers are equally noisy. Second, the only unwind that clears zero strips the squad to exactly eleven while keeping Amoako, a guaranteed zero, permanently in the eleven with almost no cash left and no legal sale available to escape; the do-nothing branch reaches the same expected points with a squad in which every player produces and real money still in hand. Third, the highest bid that could still be unwound sits barely above his market value, far below where contested listings on this board actually clear, so an affordable bid almost certainly loses and a winning bid could not be unwound at all — which would mean a negative balance at the lock and a scoreless matchday. Elsewhere: Veerman is a new manager ask and a fit, starting player, but buying him would cost both Bernardo and Lokonga out of the eleven and leave the team clearly worse, and the ask sits at roughly double the going rate for a manager listing. Kone is a new listing with no points history, no place in his club's projected eleven, and expires after the lock; he is a twelfth-body candidate, which is precisely what Georg is trying to shed. El Aynaoui stays a watch rather than a buy, and one point against him has been withdrawn — his absence from Leipzig's projected eleven is not evidence, because that page was last updated before his transfer was announced. The vacancy he was signed into is real, with two central midfielders injured, but nothing dated yet puts him in the side, and buying him would still cost more in sold players than he could plausibly return.

killed_this_run.name: Fabio Vieira (11967) — and THE UNWIND-CEILING DOCTRINE that kills every big buy at 12 players
killed_this_run.why: READ THE DOCTRINE BEFORE EVER RECOMMENDING A BUY ABOVE ~4M. Vieira is the best-looking buy the board has produced and he is still a REJECT, and the reason generalises. THE PLAYER IS GENUINELY GOOD - this is not a quality rejection. Fabio Vieira (11967), HSV (tid 6, tn "Hamburg"), pos 3 MID, st 0 fit, mv 18.586.935, cv 18.500.000, mvt 0, listed by KICKBASE (no u field) at prc = mv exactly, ofc 0, dt 2026-09-03T00:39:10Z, expiry 2026-09-04T01:07Z. HE HAS NO 26/27 POINTS ONLY BECAUSE HE WAS STILL AN ARSENAL PLAYER ON MD1 - get_player_performance confirms ph [{hp:false}] for MD1 (Dortmund 2:0 HSV 29.08). DO NOT apply the "cheap player with no history" heuristic to him and DO NOT apply the refuted 500.000 rule: he has a FULL 25/26 Bundesliga season at HSV on loan - 29 scoring appearances, 25 starts, season ap 96, tp 2795, mean 104,8 over starts, mean 108,3 over his last 13, with 217/201/195/178/177/158/157 highs. A realistic ap is 95-115. Ligainsider HSV page (stand 01.09.2026 20:31, post-MD1) names him in the probable XI at CAM v Mainz 06.09 15:30 - AFTER the MD2 lock, so he would count. THE ARITHMETIC IS WHY HE IS AN AVOID, and it was computed by brute force over every 2-sale unwind and all eight legal shapes. Doing NOTHING and just fixing the lineup gives 5-3-2 = 1395 fielded ap for free. Buying Vieira AT MV (18.586.935) takes cash 4.037.522 to MINUS 14.549.413. The squad becomes 13, so exactly TWO sales are legal before the 11-man floor. The ONLY 2-sale combo that gets the balance back to non-negative is Bernardo + Lokonga (7.048.552 + 9.748.111 = 16.796.663 -> +2.247.250), and that leaves 11 = 1/4/4/2 fielding 1385 at ap 96 or 1399 at ap 110. So the whole operation is worth MINUS 10 to PLUS 4 points against doing nothing for free. At +10% over mv it is +388.556 balance and the same 1385-1399. At +20% (the middle of the corrected Kickbase band) NO combo except selling Minjae or Matsima clears zero and the best XI drops to 1351, strictly WORSE than 1395. Adding a second cheap buy to unlock a third sale was also priced: Vieira + Ndiaye then selling Bernardo+Lokonga+Widmer gives 1370. Also worse. THE DOCTRINE, which is the durable part: SPENDING POWER IS AN ILLUSION AT 12 PLAYERS. kb_context prints spending power 54.721.905 and that number is real for the 33% floor, but it is NOT purchasing capacity, because CASH is only 4.037.522 and a negative balance at matchday start scores ZERO for the whole matchday. Every euro above cash must be earned back by SALES before the lock, and the number of sales is capped at (squad size - 11), not by what he owns. At 12 players that is ONE sale; at 13 after a buy it is TWO. His only points-free bodies are Amoako (1.709.447) and Widmer (1.853.282), so his TRUE buying capacity without touching the fielded eleven is about 4.037.522 + 1.709.447 + 1.853.282 = 7.600.251. Anything above that is paid for in fielded points, and the points a big buy adds are handed straight back by the players he must sell to unwind. THE TEST A FUTURE RUN MUST RUN BEFORE RECOMMENDING ANY BUY: price the FULLY UNWOUND end state (balance >= 0, squad >= 11, best legal XI) against the do-nothing optimum. If it does not beat it by a clear margin, it is an AVOID no matter how good the player is. HOW VIEIRA COULD BECOME A BUY: only once the squad has genuine spare bodies - 13+ players of which 2+ are droppable - or once cash is above ~15M. Neither is reachable before the 2026-09-04T18:30Z lock. ALSO AVOIDED THIS RUN, same board sweep: Moussa Ndiaye (13449), Werder DEF, mv 1.870.307, Kickbase listing at mv, expiry 2026-09-03T20:42Z, no points history and no dated news - a 12th-body candidate only, and Georg already has the 12th body he is trying to sell. NOTE ON ofc: Vieira showed ofc 0, but the listing was SIX MINUTES old at the read. A brand-new listing with ofc 0 is uninformative - the corrected ofc rule in HOLD Hntz0sp only applies to a listing that has been up long enough to attract offers. There are currently no manager asks priced below market value anywhere on the board, so the mechanism a flip depends on is simply absent — there is nothing to buy below value and resell. A full sweep of all twelve squad players against Ligainsider's league-wide injured-and-suspended table returned none of them, and a search for new stories in the last forty-eight hours across the relevant club feeds turned up no injury, suspension, benching or departure for any of them.
